doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

chapter: Reflections on Hamilton and the band
title: Drinking on campus
summary: Mead says college drinking was a big problem then and still is.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I wanted to go back to Hamilton for a moment. A lot of colleges these days have big problems with alcohol on campus. What was it like during your years here?

I think we had big problems. I think that’s one thing, I’m sure it hasn’t gotten better but I’m not sure it’s gotten worse. I think there’s always been a tremendous amount of drinking on college campuses. Certainly where I live the University of Vermont this is a problem and I think it’s a problem everyplace.
Okay. So it wasn’t so much connected to the drinking age per se, which is higher now, but did it change the issue?
I don’t think so. That’s not a very scientific answer but I don’t think so. I think we had a lot of drinking in those days.
